name: GM - Fort Wayne Assembly, Roanoke IN

fieldNotes.facility: GM Fort Wayne Assembly, Roanoke IN (former Pontiac Truck & Bus, operating since 1986). Builds the Chevrolet Silverado 1500 / GMC Sierra 1500 on the GMT T1XX platform. ~4.6M sq ft under roof on a ~716-acre site. Roster's approximate coords (40.923,-85.301) landed in farmland ~5 km south; re-pinned to the real plant complex at 40.9655,-85.2995, confirmed by the unmistakable multi-million-sq-ft assembly building, the multi-track auto-rack rail yard along the north edge, and the vast finished-vehicle storage lots ringing the plant.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Fully fenced, controlled-access GM assembly campus set well back from public roads behind wide grassy berms. A perimeter ring road circles the entire property; truck/material entrances feed from Lafayette Center Rd on the south and a separate access on the west. Standard GM plant security posture (guarded entries) inferred; Street View does not penetrate the private drives so the booth itself is not directly imaged.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Inferred from GM assembly-plant security standard and the controlled entry geometry; the booth structure is not directly resolvable in available imagery, so flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: False because a staffed guard presence is assumed at this scale of plant; if check-in is actually kiosk-based this would flip.
fieldNotes.entryExitSeparate: Large campus with multiple gate/road points (south Lafayette Center Rd entry, west material entry, plus rail) implies separate in/out flows for truck vs employee traffic.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: 50+ band: loading docks distributed across multiple faces of the assembly complex plus parts-receiving banks on the west and southwest. Trailers visibly backed in at the SW dock bank. Overhead-only estimate.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Numerous trailers staged in drop lots on the west side and along the north near the rail yard; 25-50 band of bare trailers without tractors.
fieldNotes.railServed: Multiple parallel rail tracks run the full length of the north edge of the property serving auto-rack loading of finished trucks — unambiguous in the wide and north (rail) satellite crops.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Body shops (x2), paint shop, general assembly and a sequence center form a connected multi-building manufacturing campus.
fieldNotes.multiStep: Campus-scale security: outer perimeter gate then internal plant checkpoints before docks, typical of GM assembly plants.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale clearly identified in imagery; left uncertain.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide entry aprons and generous paved width at the south entry leave room for an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Rural/edge-of-town setting: the plant is surrounded by farmland and an interstate (I-469/US-24) interchange in Roanoke, well outside Fort Wayne's dense urban fabric.
fieldNotes.geofence: Perimeter traced to the fenced property edge (rail yard north, Lafayette Center Rd / berm south, storage lots east and west). Roughly grid-aligned with a slight bend on the south and east edges. Site area ~716 acres per GM published figure.

citations.claim: GM lists Fort Wayne Assembly (Roanoke IN) as a GM-operated plant building Chevrolet Silverado 1500 / GMC Sierra 1500; celebrated 11-millionth vehicle Mar 2026
GM announced $632M investment in Fort Wayne Assembly, Roanoke IN, which produces Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra full-size pickups

verification.rationale: GM-operated light-duty truck plant, actively producing and ramping in 2026 (11M-vehicle milestone Mar 2026). Former Pontiac Truck & Bus plant: the Pontiac BRAND was wound down in 2009 but the PLANT was retained by New GM (never divested to Motors Liquidation/RACER).
